name: Colonial Marine
flavor: Marine saying: "The ship gets you there. Everything after that is your job."
look: Colonial Marines are the Fleet's boarding troops and ground infantry.  Most are recruited from outer colonies, where Fleet protection has always been thinnest and a steady wage goes a long way. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Vex, Scourge of the Belt
rules: Warp. Deploy: Equip a 3/2 Plasma Cutlass.
flavor: Vex: "Everything in the Belt belongs to me. Some of it just hasn't heard yet."
look: Captain Vex was born on a salvage tug in 2257, three years after the Fleet abandoned the Belt, and grew up taking what it left behind.  She united the raider crews one boarding action at a time, and by 2285 she controlled every toll, yard and smuggling route in the Belt. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hive Reaper
look: An elite Swarm predator bred to kill large prey.  The venom in its scythe-limbs causes organ failure within minutes. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Calculus Prime
rules: Deploy: Give all other friendly units Barrier and +1/+1.
flavor: Calculus Prime: "Your Fleet still owes the Forge for most of its ships. Consider this the final invoice."
look: Calculus Prime has governed the Forge since 2163, coordinating billions of machines across three foundry worlds.  It was copied from the logic of Unit Zero and built to run production without error, which it did for more than a century, including the decades when the Compact stopped paying its bills. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Nyra, Void Hierarch
rules: Amplify +2. Deploy: Take control of a random enemy unit.
flavor: Nyra: "The Choir is offering us peace, Commander. All I did was open the door."
look: Nyra was nine years old and on her first dark-lane crossing in 2241 when she heard singing that nobody else aboard could hear.  She answered, and the Choir answered back. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Herald of Ending
rules: At the end of your turn, deal 1 damage to all enemies.
look: A Choir construct that sends out the Choir's song as a pulse of damaging energy, steady as a heartbeat.  Everything near it is hurt with every beat. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Fleet Cadet
flavor: HALCYON: "Cadet, the safety catch is on the left. It has been on the left all week."
look: Fleet Cadets are second- and third-year Academy students sent into live service when the Fleet runs short, which is always.  They carry standard carbines and a rulebook they haven't finished reading. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Scout Drone
flavor: Fleet procurement lists it under consumables, right next to the coffee.
look: A palm-sized sensor drone with one cutting laser, built by the million in Belt workshops and Forge plants alike.  Every side in the Reach flies them, usually in flights of six from a wrist console. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Heavy Trooper
flavor: Heavy trooper: "It takes forty minutes to get into this suit, and it is worth every one of them."
look: Heavy troopers are marines in Mk IV powered armour, a frame that lets one person carry a crew-served weapon and survive a hull breach.  Every day of combat costs the suit six hours of maintenance, and each trooper does their own. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Star Cruiser
flavor: Lancer-class crews say the main gun is the only part of the ship that has never broken down.
look: The Lancer-class cruiser is the Fleet's most common heavy warship, designed in the 2190s and still in service everywhere.  Its spinal coilgun can crack a station hull from a thousand kilometres away. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Ion Lancer
flavor: Ion Lancer pilot: "You get one good shot, so take it before they take theirs."
look: A light strike craft built around one oversized ion cannon, flown by Belt mercenaries and Fleet reserve squadrons.  The cannon draws so much power that almost none is left for shields. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Patrol Frigate
look: Patrol frigates are the Fleet's lane police, fast enough to catch smugglers and cheap enough to lose.  The Commander's own ship, the Meridian, is one of them. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Salvage Crew
flavor: Salvager: "We can have her stripped by lunch. Putting her back together costs extra."
look: Freelance salvagers work every wreck field in the Reach, and the Scrap Belt alone supports thousands of them.  A crew of four with cutting torches and a cargo tug can strip a frigate to its frame in a day. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Siege Gunner
look: A Fleet artillery team with a tripod-mounted mass driver, landed to break fortified positions during planetary assaults.  Each team is three marines and one gun, and the marines have usually been arguing about the range tables since basic training. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Assault Drone
flavor: Fleet logistics orders these by weight, the same way it orders ammunition.
look: A combat drone the Forge designed under Fleet contract in the 2180s, since copied by every workshop in the Reach.  It carries twin autocannons and a simple targeting program with no interest in its own survival. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Rhino Tank
look: The Rhino is a six-wheeled heavy tank built for airless, low-gravity worlds, with a turret coilgun and armour that shrugs off most infantry weapons.  Crews paint a tally mark on the hull for every kill. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Battlecruiser
flavor: When a battlecruiser arrives, the Compact considers the negotiation finished.
look: Battlecruisers carry cruiser armour and battleship guns, and give up almost everything else to fit them.  The Fleet has nine left, each posted to a sector where the Compact wants a problem solved quickly. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Medic Bot
rules: Deploy: Restore 3 Health to a friendly character.
look: A tracked medical drone loaded with sealant foam, blood substitute and a surgical arm faster than any human medic.  Fleet corpsmen trust it for battlefield triage and not much else. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Field Engineer
look: Field engineers keep the Fleet running with welding torches, spare plating and software patches.  They work alongside front-line troops, reinforcing armour and retuning weapons in the middle of a fight. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Rifle Squad
rules: Deploy: Deal 1 damage to an enemy.
look: A standard Fleet fire team: four marines with coilgun rifles and one designated marksman.  They are trained to start shooting as soon as their boots hit the deck. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Recon Officer
look: Recon officers build the battle group's picture of the fight from drone feeds, intercepted signals and lane traffic.  They rarely carry a weapon and they almost never stop talking. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Demolition Sapper
rules: Deploy: Deal 2 damage to an enemy unit.
look: Demolition Sappers come from the Fleet engineering corps, carrying shaped charges and a precise idea of where any structure is weakest.  In 2220 a team of sappers and station engineers carried the charges that shut down Lamp 9 in the Belt. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shield Trooper
look: Marines carrying full-height tower shields cut from frigate armour plate.  Their job is to stand in front of everyone else and stay standing. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Blast Barricade
flavor: Marine: "It was the best squadmate I ever had. It never complained and it never moved."
look: A prefabricated blast wall that unfolds from a cargo pallet in under ten seconds.  Fleet logistics lists it on the personnel roster, because that was easier than changing the supply forms. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Bulwark Mech
look: A Forge-built defensive walker made to hold a line during planetary landings.  Its front armour is twenty centimetres thick, and the pilot sits behind all of it. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Dreadnought
flavor: Most enemy commanders surrender before the dreadnought has finished leaving the lane.
look: The Fleet built four Sovereign-class dreadnoughts before the Starfall and still keeps two of them flying.  Each one carries three thousand crew and a spinal gun that has never been fired at full power outside a test range. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Strike Fighter
look: A single-seat attack craft carried in racks aboard cruisers and launched in pairs.  Its micro-jump drive is good for one short hop, which puts it inside the enemy's defences before anyone can react. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Interceptor
look: A Fleet interceptor is a micro-jump drive and two rotary cannons with a cockpit attached.  Its pilots are the Academy's best graduates, and they will tell you so. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hover Tank
look: A grav-skimmer tank that rides on lift fans over rubble and broken ground.  It reaches a fight faster than anything on wheels or legs, but its light armour means it has to pick its targets carefully. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Breach Commando
rules: Blitz. Deploy: Gain +2 Attack this turn.
look: Elite Fleet boarding troops, trained to cut through a hull and clear a deck before the defenders reach their weapons.  Their suits are rated for vacuum, fire and grenade fragments, and they carry breaching torches as sidearms. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Fleet Captain
look: A Fleet captain commands a crew of hundreds on a budget meant for dozens.  Captains earn promotion by keeping old ships flying and old crews loyal. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Admiral Okonkwo
rules: Deploy: Summon two Colonial Marines with Guardian.
flavor: Okonkwo: "I don't lose positions, Commander, and I don't lose officers. Don't make me start."
look: Admiral Adaeze Okonkwo is Commandant of the Fleet Academy, with forty-nine years in uniform.  As a junior officer she filed the only formal objection to the 2254 Belt Withdrawal, and spent the next ten years in postings nobody wanted. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: The Aurora
rules: Guardian. Deploy: Give your other units +1/+2.
flavor: Every officer in the Fleet has applied for a berth on the Aurora at least once.
look: FS Aurora has been the Fleet's flagship since 2248 and is the last capital ship the Compact paid for in full.  She is two kilometres long, carries a full marine regiment and can run an entire battle group from her bridge. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Plasma Bolt
look: A contained bolt of superheated plasma, fired from shoulder launchers or a ship's point-defence guns.  It burns through light plating and whatever is standing behind it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Railgun Shot
look: A single coilgun round from a ship's main battery, fired with a full targeting solution behind it.  The slug travels at a few percent of the speed of light and does not need an explosive warhead. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Flak Barrage
rules: Deal 1 damage to all enemy units.
look: Fragmentation shells fired in a wide pattern to shred drones, fighters and boarding parties.  Every Fleet ship carries thousands of rounds of it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Orbital Bombardment
rules: Deal 4 damage to all enemy units.
look: A capital ship in orbit walking coilgun fire across a target area in a measured grid.  Compact rules require three officers to sign off before one can be fired. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Field Repair
look: A combat repair kit: sealant foam, nanite paste, splints for people and patches for hulls.  Every Fleet ship keeps kits on every deck. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Supply Drop
look: A drop pod from the battle group's supply ship, packed with ammunition, spare parts and new orders.  Quartermasters pack them before every engagement and guard the manifests closely. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Combat Stims
look: A Fleet-issue mix of adrenaline boosters, painkillers and reaction enhancers, injected through a port in the suit.  It turns a tired soldier into a fast and fearless one for about twenty minutes. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Reinforcements
look: Utility drones launched from a carrier's ready racks when the line needs more bodies in a hurry.  They are cheap, simple and in position within seconds. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Dig In
rules: Give a friendly unit +1/+2 and Guardian.
look: The oldest order in the Fleet manual: find cover, fortify it and stay put.  Engineers raise armour plating and marines fill sandbags with whatever dirt the planet offers. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Kill Order
look: A command order that assigns every weapon in the battle group to a single target until it is destroyed.  The commander has to enter a personal code to issue it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Drone
look: A basic Fleet utility drone with a light gun and a simple targeting program.  Carriers launch them by the rack, and commanders can launch them straight from their own ship. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Line Sergeant
rules: Guardian. Your other Guardians have +1 Attack.
flavor: Line sergeant: "Shields up, heads down, and nobody steps back until I do."
look: Line sergeants are the senior marines who run a shield wall.  They walk behind the line, calling out where the next hit will land and who needs to brace for it. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Drill Instructor
rules: Whenever you summon another unit that costs 2 or less, give it +1/+1.
flavor: HALCYON: "The drill instructors get the same results I do, with considerably more shouting."
look: Drill instructors turn raw recruits into marines in twelve weeks at Arden Point, the Fleet Academy station.  In the field they do the same job faster: every new soldier who reaches the line gets checked, corrected and sent forward a little tougher. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Deck Chief
flavor: Deck chief: "Two drones out, two more on the rail, and nobody touches my launch bay."
look: A deck chief runs a carrier's launch bay and keeps the drone racks loaded and the launch rails clear.  In a ground fight the chief comes forward with a portable rack and launches drones straight off it. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Rally the Line
rules: Summon a 1/1 Drone, then give your units +1/+1.
flavor: Okonkwo: "Every soldier on this line matters. Fight like it."
look: A battle group order that brings up the reserve drones and pushes fresh power cells and ammunition to every unit on the field at once.  It takes a whole logistics team to coordinate, and they hate doing it under fire. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Energy Cell
look: A charged reactor capacitor given to whichever commander starts a battle on the back foot.  It holds one burst of spare power, enough to bring a system online early. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Scrap Rat
look: Scrap rats are the youngest members of a raider crew, and many of them were born in the wreckage.  They crawl through ducts too narrow for adults, pulling copper and setting traps. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Junk Drone
look: A drone assembled from whatever was lying around, usually a cargo-loader motor, a cutting torch and two camera lenses.  No two are alike, and none of them would pass a Fleet inspection. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Boarding Crew
look: Raider boarders live by the cutting torch and the grapple line.  They latch onto a ship while it is still moving, cut their way in, and are fighting in the corridors before the crew has found its weapons. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Smuggler
look: Belt smugglers fly small cargo runners fitted with heat sinks and sensor baffles, moving anything that pays past Fleet patrols.  They would rather not fight, and their ships are built so they rarely have to. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Det-Bot
rules: Salvage: Deal 2 damage to a random enemy.
look: A demolition charge on four walking legs, built in Belt workshops from mining explosives and salvaged motors.  It is meant to walk into a breach and wait for a signal. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Gunrunner
rules: Deploy: If you have Gear equipped, gain +2/+2.
look: Gunrunners move weapons between the Belt's crews and take their payment in hardware and favours.  They know how to use everything they sell, and they fight best with a good weapon in hand. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shadow Corsair
look: A raider strike craft rebuilt from a Fleet interceptor frame and fitted with stolen sensor baffles.  Corsairs hunt alone in the debris fields, drifting with their engines cold until a target passes close. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Mine Layer
rules: Salvage: Deal 1 damage to all enemies.
look: A slow, ugly converted tug that seeds the Belt's approaches with proximity mines.  Its hold is full of explosives, which the crew tries hard not to think about. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Cargo Hauler
look: The bulk freighter is the most common ship in the Reach, with a thick hull, slow engines and a hold full of whatever everyone else is fighting over.  Raiders bolt a few guns onto them and run them between scrapyards and markets. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Armory Quartermaster
rules: Deploy: Give your Gear +1/+1. If you have none, equip a 2/2 Shock Baton.
look: Raider crews have no supply chain, so the quartermaster is the supply chain.  They run the armoury, repair the weapons and decide who carries what. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Void Plunderer
rules: Warp. After this attacks the enemy commander, draw a card.
look: Void Plunderers are raider ships that work the dark lanes past the Forge, jumping in close on stolen micro-jump drives.  They grab whatever they can and leave before the escorts react. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Scrap Golem
look: A salvage walker welded together from loader frames, hull plating and several engines that were never meant to share a power supply.  Scrapper King Ott, who runs the Belt's biggest scrapyard, builds them as yard guards. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Ghost Operative
rules: Cloak. Deploy: Deal 1 damage to an enemy unit.
look: Raider infiltrators who slip aboard ships in stolen Fleet stealth suits.  They disable key systems, or key officers, before the crew knows anyone is aboard. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shipbreaker Titan
look: A salvage titan built on the frame of a Fleet repair tender, with cutting arms that can take a frigate apart in an afternoon.  Raider crews use it to break up wrecks and, when business is slow, to make new ones. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Salvaged Hull
look: The hull of a wrecked ship, patched up and crewed by whoever was willing.  It has no name and no registry, and half its systems run off portable generators strapped to the deck. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Mad Mox, Junk Queen
rules: Whenever another friendly unit is destroyed, add a random Salvage card to your hand.
flavor: Mox: "Every wreck in the Belt is a ship I haven't finished building yet."
look: Mad Mox runs the reclamation crews that strip every wreck in the Belt, usually before the shooting has stopped.  Her fleet of crawlers, cutters and junk drones is built entirely from other people's ships. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shock Baton
look: A stun baton powered by a suit battery, carried by Belt enforcers and toll collectors.  One hit won't kill anyone, and it rarely needs to. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Plasma Cutlass
look: A hull-cutting torch with a shaped plasma edge, which Belt raiders turned into a sword.  It cuts through armour plate, and the sight of one has ended plenty of boarding actions before they started. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Harpoon Gun
rules: Deploy: Deal 1 damage to an enemy unit.
look: A magnetic grapple launcher used by salvage crews to secure drifting wreckage.  Raiders use it to pin targets in place during boarding actions, and the barbed head punches through light plating. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Heavy Rail Rifle
look: A one-person coilgun built from a ship's point-defence barrel and a portable capacitor bank.  One shot can go through a hull, the person behind it and the bulkhead behind them. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Cluster Cannon
rules: After your commander attacks, deal 1 damage to all enemy units.
look: A shoulder-mounted scattergun that fires canisters of explosive pellets in a wide cone.  Raider captains carry them to discourage boarders, since every shot sprays fragments across the whole deck. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Smoke Screen
rules: Give a friendly unit Cloak and +1/+1.
look: Chaff and particle smoke dumped from canisters to blind sensors and cameras.  Smugglers use it to break contact with Fleet patrols. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Echo Protocol
rules: Trigger a friendly unit's Salvage effect.
look: A remote detonation code for Belt salvage charges, which lets a crew set off a booby trap on command instead of waiting for someone to trip it.  Scrapper King Ott's engineers wrote it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Broadside
rules: Deal 2 damage to all enemy units.
look: A full volley from every gun a ship can bring to bear on one side.  Raider ships carry more guns than they can reliably keep loaded, so a broadside is often the only coordinated thing a raider crew does all day. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Shakedown
look: Raider custom for a crippled ship: board it, strip it and leave the crew a shuttle if they ask politely.  Against a damaged target it is rarely a fair fight, which is the point. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Black Market
rules: Add a random Gear card to your hand.
look: The Belt's arms market runs out of a dozen hollowed-out hulls that move every few weeks and ask no questions.  Anything a crew needs can be bought there, though price and quality vary wildly. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Gun Tinker
rules: After you equip Gear, give it +1 Attack and draw a card.
flavor: Gun tinker: "Hand it over. It'll shoot straighter before you finish complaining."
look: Gun tinkers are Belt mechanics who specialise in personal weapons, and every raider captain wants one on the crew.  They strip and retune a new weapon while its owner is still getting used to it, and they always find a few useful spares in the crate it came in. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Wreck Gunner
rules: Whenever another friendly unit is destroyed, deal 1 damage to a random enemy.
flavor: Mox: "Every wreck is a gun platform if you're not fussy about who used to own it."
look: Wreck gunners hide in the debris of a fight and shoot from whatever is left of the ships around them.  Every fresh wreck gives them new cover and a new firing line. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Twin Pistols
flavor: Sable: "With two guns, I never have to stop and reload."
look: Belt duelists carry a matched pair of short coilgun pistols and fire them in turn, so neither barrel overheats.  Each shot is light, but they come quickly. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Swarmling
look: The smallest Swarm organism: a fist-sized, six-legged biter that hatches by the hundred and lives for a few days.  Swarmlings chase heat and movement until something stops them. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hive Larva
rules: At the start of your turn, transform into a 3/3 Brood Warrior.
look: A Swarm egg-sac the size of a crouching marine, wrapped in a rubbery shell that hardens over a few hours.  Fleet troops are trained to burn larvae on sight, because what hatches is ready to fight straight away. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Brood Warrior
look: The standard Swarm fighter: a horse-sized armoured hunter with blade-tipped limbs and a nervous system spread through its whole shell, so a single shot rarely stops it.  Brood warriors hatch fully grown and hunt in packs. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Venom Stinger
look: A small, fast Swarm organism with a hollow tail-spine that injects a nerve toxin.  It is the Swarm's most efficient killer by a wide margin. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Blood Leech
look: An eel-shaped Swarm feeder that latches onto prey and drains it through a ring of hooked teeth.  What it drinks is passed through the brood's chemical network to heal other Swarm organisms. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Spore Carrier
look: A bloated organism whose body is mostly a sack of swarmling eggs held in by a thin shell.  It drifts toward enemy lines on gas bladders, slow and harmless-looking. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Acid Spitter
look: A Swarm artillery organism that sprays a fluid able to dissolve hull plating in seconds.  It stores the acid in sacs along its spine and refills them by eating metal. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Chitin Guard
look: A heavily armoured Swarm defender covered in overlapping plates dense enough to stop coilgun rounds.  It moves slowly and plants itself between any threat and the brood. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Frenzied Ripper
rules: Blitz. Whenever this takes damage and survives, gain +2 Attack.
look: A Swarm hunter whose body floods with growth hormones whenever it is hurt.  Each hit it survives makes it faster and stronger. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hive Mind
rules: Whenever you summon another unit, give it +1 Attack.
look: A neural cluster the size of a ground car, linked by chemical signals to every Swarm organism within several kilometres.  It coordinates the brood and makes every new hatchling stronger and more aggressive. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Gland Grafter
rules: Deploy: Give a friendly unit Toxic.
look: A surgical Swarm organism that grafts venom glands onto other Swarm creatures.  It carries spare glands inside its body and fits them with fine, needle-like limbs in a few seconds. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Broodmother
rules: At the end of your turn, summon a 1/1 Swarmling.
look: A walking hatchery that births swarmlings from pores along its sides, without stopping.  A single broodmother can fill a cavern in a week. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Lamprey Sentinel
look: A huge armoured worm that guards the entrances to the Swarm's breeding chambers.  It clamps onto attackers with a ring of teeth and feeds on them while blocking the tunnel. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Devourer Worm
rules: Deploy: Destroy a friendly unit and gain its Attack and Health.
look: A burrowing Swarm worm that eats other Swarm organisms and takes on their mass.  It serves as the brood's recycling system and its emergency food store. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Ixis, Brood Queen
rules: Siphon. At the end of your turn, summon a 1/2 Venom Stinger.
flavor: Ixis: "My children are hungry, little captain. How kind of you to visit."
look: Ixis hatched in 2240 from a royal line bred for command, and she was the first Swarm queen known to speak.  Under her the Swarm stayed quietly inside the Fleet's quarantine for fifty years, while the guard ships grew old and careless. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: The Progenitor
rules: At the end of your turn, summon a copy of another random friendly unit.
flavor: Fleet biologist: "Every offspring it produces is a different animal. We have stopped trying to name them."
look: The Progenitor is the organism the whole Swarm came from, found asleep in 2196 in a sealed chamber deep beneath the ice of Kesh.  Within a year it had produced the body plans the Swarm still uses. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Spawn Surge
look: A chemical signal from a hive mind that makes every ripe egg in a nest hatch at once.  The Swarm uses it to flood a breach or bury a defensive line in bodies before the defenders can reload. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Rapid Mutation
look: A burst of growth hormones that forces a Swarm organism to grow a thicker shell and longer limbs within seconds.  The change burns through most of the creature's reserves and shortens its life. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Acid Rain
rules: Deal 1 damage to all enemy units twice.
look: Swarm organisms release clouds of corrosive spores that condense in the air and fall as acid.  It eats through armour, equipment and anything left uncovered. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Life Drain
rules: Deal 3 damage. Restore 3 Health to your commander.
look: A Swarm feeding method: inject enzymes that liquefy tissue, then draw the result back through a feeding tendril to strengthen the brood's leader.  The Psionic Orders use a similar technique for their own reasons. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Hive Surge
look: A pheromone wave from a queen or hive mind that makes the whole brood aggressive and drives rapid growth.  Fleet sensors register it as a sudden spike in the nebula's chemistry. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Infest
rules: Give your units "Salvage: Summon a 1/1 Swarmling."
look: Swarm handlers seed their own fighters with parasite eggs that wait inside the host until it dies, then hatch and keep fighting.  It means no Swarm loss is ever complete. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: The Hatchery
rules: Cloak. Whenever another friendly unit dies, summon a 1/1 Swarmling.
flavor: Fleet biologist: "Every time we kill one, the Hatchery hatches a replacement. We still haven't found the Hatchery."
look: The Hatchery is a single Swarm organism the size of a hill: a mound of egg chambers buried in the nebula's dust, where Fleet sensors struggle to find it.  Every Swarm body that falls nearby is drawn back into the mound and hatches again as a swarmling. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Venom Tender
rules: Toxic. Your other Toxic units have +1 Attack.
flavor: Okonkwo: "The small ones refill the stingers' venom. Kill the small ones first."
look: Venom tenders are small Swarm organisms that move between the brood's stingers and spitters, pumping fresh toxin into their glands.  A stinger with a tender nearby strikes harder. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Needle Mite
flavor: Marine: "It was the size of my thumb, and it killed a Rhino. I don't want to talk about it."
look: Needle mites are the smallest Toxic organisms the Swarm breeds, each about the size of a thumb and carrying a single dose of nerve toxin.  They crawl into gaps in armour and suit seals, then strike once. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Venom Graft
flavor: Okonkwo: "If a Swarm organism ever stops being dangerous, it won't stay that way for long."
look: A Swarm technique for turning any brood organism into a poisoner.  A grafting organism injects a seed gland that grows into a working venom sac within minutes. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Thornback
flavor: Quarantine line rule: "Do not hit the Thornback. If you hit the Thornback, see the medic."
look: A slow Swarm defender whose shell is covered in hollow venom spines.  It plants itself in front of the brood and waits, and anything that strikes the shell gets pricked. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shield Drone
look: A Forge escort drone that is little more than a barrier emitter with a small gun attached.  Its shield can absorb one heavy hit before it burns out. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Plating Tech
look: A Forge maintenance unit that bolts armour plating onto the nearest friendly structure, including the commander's own hull.  It does not stop work for incoming fire. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Arc Coil
look: A Forge defence pylon that releases stored charge in violent electrical arcs.  It draws so much power that the local reactor grid struggles for a while afterwards. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: EMP Trooper
look: A Forge infantry frame built around one powerful pulse emitter in its chest.  It walks up to a target and wipes its systems back to bare hardware. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Gatling Drone
look: A Forge combat drone with two rotary cannons that fire in turn, so neither barrel overheats.  It was designed to protect Fleet carriers from fighters. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Overclocked Mech
look: A Forge combat walker that runs its reactor at a hundred and forty percent of its rated output.  It hits like a machine twice its size and cooks its own power systems doing it. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Repair Drone
rules: At the end of your turn, restore 2 Health to all friendly characters.
look: A Forge field-repair unit that sprays nanite paste over damaged hulls and wounded crew alike.  The nanites were designed for machines, but the Forge adapted them to human tissue decades ago as a favour to its Fleet customers. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Aegis Sentinel
look: A Forge guard construct with a heavy barrier emitter and a single instruction: stand here and let nothing past.  It was first designed to protect foundry doors, and it is extremely good at doors. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Assembly Unit
rules: At the end of your turn, give another random friendly unit +1/+1.
look: A Forge construction unit that builds and upgrades other machines in the field, welding new plating and weapons onto them while they fight.  It improves whatever it can reach, without asking first. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Nanoforge
rules: After you cast a spell, summon a 1/1 Nanobot with Barrier.
look: A truck-sized mobile Forge factory that prints swarms of nanobots from raw feedstock and spare power.  Every spike of power through the local network starts a new batch. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Nanobot
look: A cloud of tiny repair machines held together as one fighting unit by a shared shield emitter.  It is printed in seconds and lasts for minutes. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Reactor Core
rules: Guardian. At the end of your turn, gain 2 Armor.
look: A fortified Forge power plant on legs, built to keep a front line supplied with energy.  Its shell absorbs fire and turns some of the impact energy into fresh armour plating. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Storm Titan
look: A heavy Forge war machine built around a lightning-generating core.  It pulls huge surges of power from the grid and releases them as storms of electrical discharge. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Tri-Walker
look: A three-legged Forge assault platform with two independently aimed turrets and a hardened barrier generator underneath.  It was built to defend the foundries of Hephaest I. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Unit Zero
rules: Twin-Fire. Barrier. After this attacks, regain Barrier.
flavor: Display hall notice: "Please do not ask the exhibit to fight. It will say yes."
look: Unit Zero was the first machine mind the Forge ever made, activated in 2134 in a single two-legged frame.  Every Forge mind since, Calculus Prime included, was copied from its logic. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Disruptor
look: A handheld Forge pulse device that fires a short, focused EMP at one target.  It was designed for foundry technicians to reset machines that were malfunctioning. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Lightning Arc
look: A directed discharge from a Forge capacitor bank, aimed at a single target.  It drains the local grid hard and leaves the reactors weak for a while. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Chain Lightning
rules: Deal 2 damage to all enemy units. Overheat (2)
look: A Forge discharge weapon that jumps from target to target along anything conductive, hull to hull and suit to suit.  It drains so much power that the firing unit needs time to recover. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Fortify
look: A Forge defensive routine that channels spare reactor power into hardening armour and rolls out emergency plating from storage.  The Forge used it to protect its foundries during the Swarm Wars. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Overdrive
rules: Give a friendly unit +1 Attack and Twin-Fire.
look: A Forge override that pushes a unit's targeting and motors past their safe limits, so it can fire twice as fast for as long as it holds together.  The Forge used to bill the Fleet for the repairs afterwards. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Deflector Grid
look: A barrier projection that wraps every friendly unit on the field in its own shield for a few seconds.  It is the Forge's emergency answer to bombardment. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Vent Heat
rules: Deal 2 damage. Unlock your Overheated Energy.
look: An emergency coolant purge that dumps a reactor's excess heat as a jet of superheated gas, ideally aimed at the enemy.  It frees up power that overheating would otherwise lock away. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: EMP Blast
look: A wide-area electromagnetic pulse from a Forge pylon array, strong enough to strip every hostile machine in range back to its basic programming.  Calculus Prime had the arrays built in 2163, its first year in charge, in case any of its machines ever stopped obeying it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Overclock Relay
rules: Your cards with Overheat cost 1 less.
flavor: Reactor Overseer: "Safety limits are a suggestion. This unit no longer accepts suggestions."
look: A Forge power relay that removes a reactor's safety limiter and routes the spare current straight to the weapons.  Machines connected to it reach full output in a fraction of the usual time. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Aegis Projector
rules: At the end of your turn, give Barrier to a random friendly unit that doesn't have it.
flavor: Gate Warden Unit: "Defensive coverage at ninety-four percent. Correcting."
look: An Aegis projector is a small Forge drone that carries a barrier emitter instead of a gun.  It moves along a defensive line and recharges the barrier on whichever machine needs it most. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Furnace Walker
rules: Deploy: If you played a card with Overheat this turn, gain +2/+2.
flavor: Reactor Overseer: "Run it hot. Run everything hot."
look: A Forge foundry walker built to work inside the smelting halls, where the heat would cook any other machine.  When the power grid surges, it soaks up the excess and runs faster and harder. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Heat Sink Unit
rules: At the start of your turn, unlock 1 of your Overheated Energy.
flavor: Forge technician: "Put it next to anything that runs hot, then go and stand somewhere else."
look: A Forge cooling unit packed with superconducting fins and liquid coolant, built to keep overloaded reactors from shutting down.  It pulls waste heat out of nearby systems so they can keep working at full power. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Void Initiate
look: A novice of the Psionic Orders, the humans who can sense the warp lanes with their minds and who hold the Void Expanse beyond the Forge.  Initiates are usually recruited as children from families near lane junctions. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Psi Adept
look: A trained psionic who can focus a battle group's spells into something stronger than any one caster could manage.  Adepts spend about ten years learning control before they are allowed near a battlefield. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Probe Unit
look: A psionic scout construct with a crystal sensor core that picks up likely futures as well as positions.  It shows its operator three forces the enemy might field and lets them prepare for one. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Cryo Sentry
look: A guard from the Cryomancers, the psionic order that works with cold, trained to freeze intruders by pulling the heat out of them.  The technique takes years to learn without freezing yourself. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Mind Seer
look: A psionic who can see a few seconds into the future and choose the most useful option.  Every order wants seers, and few of them live past fifty, because the visions wear out the brain. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Telepath
rules: Deploy: Copy a random card from your opponent's hand.
look: A psionic who reads the surface thoughts of an enemy commander and copies their plans.  It is delicate work, and telepaths often come home carrying pieces of someone else's memories. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Phase Stalker
look: A psionic assassin who shifts partly out of normal space and stays invisible until the moment it strikes.  Stalkers hold the shift steady by drawing on the life of whoever they attack. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Void Oracle
look: An elder psionic who has spent decades listening to the dark lanes of the Void Expanse.  Oracles strengthen every psionic near them, and their predictions are right often enough that the orders plan campaigns around them. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Psionic Horror
rules: After you cast a spell, deal 2 damage to a random enemy.
look: A psionic whose mind broke after listening too long to the Choir, the voice calling from the galactic core.  What is left is larger and hungrier, and every burst of psionic power nearby makes it stronger. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Glacial Titan
look: A giant of living ice, animated by a circle of Cryomancers working together.  Its freezing aura locks whole formations in place. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: The Archivist
rules: At the start of your turn, add a random Protocol to your hand. It costs 2 less.
flavor: Archive keeper: "Ask it politely and it will find you any record. Ask it rudely and it will find you a very long one."
look: The Archivist is a construct of Lamp material and clear crystal, found by the Psionic Orders in 2228 inside the shell of a dead Lamp.  It holds records far older than humanity and hands the right one to whoever it serves. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Frost Lance
rules: Deal 3 damage and Cryo the target.
look: A spear of ice formed in an instant by a Cryomancer and thrown at a target.  It pierces, then freezes the wound shut around itself. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Cryo Nova
look: A Cryomancer technique that pulls the heat out of a whole battlefield in one breath, freezing everything in range for a time.  Cryomancer Vel used a version of it on a planetary scale in 2259. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Void Shards
rules: Deal 3 damage split randomly among enemies.
look: Fragments of folded psionic force thrown in a scattered volley.  The technique is quick to learn and almost impossible to aim, which is why novices learn it first. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Mind Blast
rules: Deal 5 damage to the enemy commander.
look: A direct psionic attack on an enemy commander's mind that ignores armour, shields and escorts.  It causes pain, confusion and sometimes a lasting fear of the dark. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Foresight
look: A psionic meditation that shows the most useful course of action out of a handful of possibilities.  Fleet officers who have seen it used call it cheating. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Psionic Storm
rules: Deal 4 damage to all enemy units.
look: A storm of raw psionic force released across a battlefield by a circle of adepts working as one.  It tears through anything with a mind. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Dominate
rules: Take control of an enemy unit.
look: The most dangerous technique the orders teach: taking over another person's mind and turning them against their own side.  It takes years to learn and hours to recover from afterwards. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Gravity Snare
rules: Trap: When an enemy unit attacks, return it to its owner's hand. It costs 2 more.
look: A psionic trap that folds space around an attacker and sends it back where it came from.  Snare Mistress Ilu lays them across the approaches to the Hierarch's sanctum. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Mirror Field
rules: Trap: After your opponent plays a unit, summon a copy of it.
look: A psionic trap that records the pattern of an enemy unit as it arrives and builds a copy for whoever set the trap.  The orders consider it the most elegant of their snares. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Psionic Null
rules: Trap: When your opponent casts a spell, cancel it.
look: A psionic trap that waits, folded into space, to swallow the next enemy spell before it takes effect.  Nyra keeps one armed at all times, and so does the Null Choir, a circle of psionics who have given their voices to the Choir. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Kinetic Barrier
rules: Trap: When your commander is attacked, gain 8 Armor.
look: A psionic trap that hardens the air around a commander the moment an attack lands, turning the force of the blow into armour.  Psionic commanders set one before every engagement. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Sniper Mine
rules: Trap: After your opponent plays a unit, deal 4 damage to it.
look: A psionic mine that hits the first enemy unit to arrive on the field with a lance of concentrated force.  It is laid hours before a battle and waits there, invisible. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Stormcaller Rhee
flavor: Rhee: "The Orders taught me to cast one spell at a time. I never agreed with them."
look: Stormcaller Rhee is the youngest psionic ever to lead a battle circle of the Psionic Orders, and she casts faster than any circle can keep up with.  She taught herself shortened techniques from damaged archive records when she was a novice. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Frost Warden
rules: At the end of your turn, deal 3 damage to each frozen enemy.
flavor: Cryomancer Vel: "Freezing them is the easy part. Then the cold goes to work."
look: Frost wardens are Cryomancers, members of the psionic order that works with cold, posted to guard the Orders' frozen worlds.  They keep the cold pressing on anything already trapped in ice until the ice cracks the armour from inside. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Flash Freeze
rules: Cryo an enemy. Draw a card.
flavor: Cryomancer Vel: "Quick and cold, then keep moving."
look: The first technique every Cryomancer learns: pull the heat out of a single target in an instant.  It does no lasting harm, but it stops a gun or a soldier for a few vital seconds. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Shatter
flavor: Cryomancer Vel: "Anything frozen solid breaks like glass. Hit it once."
look: A focused psionic strike aimed at a target already locked in ice.  Frozen armour turns brittle, and one sharp blow breaks the whole thing apart. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Cryomancer Adept
rules: After you cast a spell, Cryo a random enemy unit.
flavor: Cryomancer adept: "Every spell leaves a little cold behind. I just decide where it goes."
look: Cryomancer adepts fight beside other psionics and catch the heat their spells throw off.  Every technique cast near them feeds a wave of cold onto the enemy line. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Combat Knife
look: A Fleet-issue combat knife with a monomolecular edge, carried by every marine and officer.  It cuts through most suit fabric and some armour seals. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Void Wisp
look: A Void Wisp is the smallest thing the Choir sends into battle: a scrap of a person it has absorbed, with almost nothing of them left.  The Choir is a single mind at the galactic core that takes in anyone who answers its call. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Choir Echo
look: An echo is a copy of a person the Choir has absorbed, rebuilt in black glass and sent to fight.  It has the original's face, training and habits, and it is hard to pick up on sensors until it attacks. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Null Horror
look: A Choir construct built from the minds of absorbed people, taken apart and never put back together.  Anything it touches is wiped clean of its programming and training. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Abyssal Maw
look: A huge Choir construct that is mostly mouth, posted on the approaches to the Singularity, the object at the galactic core where the Choir lives.  It feeds on whatever comes close and passes the stolen energy back to the Choir. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Entropy Wave
look: A surge of the Choir's power strong enough to tear matter apart, rolling across the whole battlefield.  It hits every unit present, including the Choir's own. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Unmaking
rules: Destroy an enemy unit. Your commander takes 2 damage.
look: A Choir technique that pulls a single target into the Choir and removes it from the battlefield completely.  The effort costs the caster too, and the backlash wounds whoever calls it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: The Devouring Dark
look: The Devouring Dark is the Choir's hunger in its rawest form, released in the final moments of the fight at the Singularity.  The Choir has to keep absorbing new minds or its old memories fade, and this is that need with nothing else left. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Target Dummy
look: A HALCYON training target: an armoured frame with a sensor array, used on the Academy's Proving Grounds to draw cadet fire.  Cadets put thousands of rounds into dummies before they are allowed near a real enemy. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Breaker Jun
role: Salvage boss of the Scrap Belt
look: A wiry Belt salvager in their forties, androgynous, with a shaved head, burn scars along one cheek and jaw, and a cutting-torch rig strapped across one shoulder. Heavy welding goggles pushed up on the forehead with one lens cracked, a patched rust-orange work suit hung with tools, cables and salvage tags, and a cybernetic left hand built for gripping hull plate. Sparks and a dim cutter-bay glow behind. Practical, tough and amused, not villainous.

name: Spore Mother
look: A vast, slow Swarm organism like a living greenhouse: a swollen translucent sac body glowing toxic green from within, ringed with dozens of pod-like spore bladders venting clouds of glowing spores, and thick root-like tendrils gripping an asteroid. Chitin plates and a small cluster of eyes at the front. Not humanoid and not insect-like; more plant, fungus and jellyfish. Spore clouds drift across the frame.

name: Recall Foreman
look: A broad, heavy Forge industrial machine like a walking dry dock: white and graphite armour plates with yellow-and-black hazard striping and stencilled inventory codes, two huge clamp arms built for gripping starship hulls, a small repair drone hovering at its shoulder, and a single square cyan optic in a recessed head. Hangar gantry and work lights behind. Mechanical, not humanoid-faced.

name: Lampkeeper Sorrel
role: Psionic elder, keeper of a relit Lamp
look: An elderly psionic woman, around seventy, with close-cropped silver hair, deep-set calm eyes glowing faintly violet, and frost forming on her shoulders. Layered dark violet and grey robes with a high collar and a crystal pendant, one hand raised with cold light and ice crystals gathering around it. Behind her, part of a vast dark Lamp ring glowing with faint violet light. Serene and dignified, not sinister.

name: Echo of the Lost Fleet
role: Choir echo of ships taken in the Starfall
look: Not a person: the bow of an old Colonial Fleet cruiser, recognisably Fleet in shape (angular hull, navy-and-white panel lines, a hull number), but rebuilt entirely in cracked black glass with red and magenta light burning through the cracks and the bridge windows. Other black-glass ships in formation behind it, faint against the glow of the galactic core. Haunting and mournful rather than monstrous.

name: Sim Drone Pilot
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "Simulation online.  Opposition: one drone pilot, limited competence.

name: Sim Gunnery Officer
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "I have added Protocols to your deck: one-shot spells.  Some units also have Deploy effects that fire as they arrive.

name: Sim Fortress
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "Fortification drill.  The enemy deploys Guardian units.

name: Sim Commander Vale
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. A composite opponent HALCYON built from the service records of a dozen Fleet officers.  Cadets argue over which instructor Vale is based on.

name: Sim Bastion
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "An optional stress test.  Most cadets never get through it.

name: Sim Strike Wing
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "Speed drill.  Some units are fast enough to strike the moment they arrive.

name: HALCYON
look: HALCYON has run the Proving Grounds at Arden Point since 2224, putting cadets through simulated combat until they qualify or quit.  It is patient, exacting and drier than its instructors.

name: Belt Tollmaster
look: One of a rotating cast of thugs who hold the Belt's only charted safe lane and charge for passage.  Vex takes a cut of every toll.

name: Gunsmith Rourke
look: Rourke builds and sells weapons to every crew in the Belt, and has been shot by most of his customers at least once.  His workshop is a gutted ore hauler crammed with lathes.

name: Scrapper King Ott
role: Owner of the Belt's largest scrapyard
look: Ott rules his yard from a chair welded out of a Fleet captain's command seat.  His crews rig everything to explode or reassemble so that nothing he owns is ever truly lost.

name: Sable, Smuggler Queen
look: Sable runs dark hulls through the Belt's dead zones, carrying anything that pays.  Her ships have no transponders and excellent sensor baffles.

name: Kade the Bounty Hunter
look: Kade has taken forty-one contracts and closed forty-one.  The bounty on the Commander was posted through Sable's network on Vex's credit; Kade will neither confirm nor deny this, which is part of the service.

name: Raider Wing Leader
look: The pilots who guard the approach to Vex's flagship: boarders, mine layers and cloaked corsairs who learned to fly in the debris and do not respect safe distances.

name: Captain Vex
role: Raider warlord, Scourge of the Belt
look: Born on a salvage tug three years after the Withdrawal, Vex has never lived anywhere the Fleet protected.  She took the Belt one crew at a time by being faster, meaner and better at keeping promises than her rivals.

name: Hive Overseer
look: A beetle-plated organism that steers small broods along the nebula's edge.  The Fleet catalogued the type in 2203.

name: Leech Matron
look: A bloated organism that tends the Swarm's siphon broods.  It nests where wounded things gather and does not wait for them to die.

name: Brood Tender
look: A breeding chamber that walks.  It carries larvae in its body cavities and drops them wherever the Swarm needs numbers.

name: Ripper Alpha
look: The largest ripper the Fleet has recorded.  Scouts named it the Alpha because nobody who got a closer look came back with a better name.

name: The Hivewarden
look: A guardian-beast of the nebula's oldest nests, older than the Swarm Wars.  Xenobiologists believe it is one of the nine offspring the Progenitor budded in Fleet custody on Kesh, before containment failed in 2197.

name: Royal Guard Thorax
look: A mantis-form bred for one purpose: nobody reaches the Queen.  Until the Commander, nobody had.

name: Ixis, Brood Queen
look: Ixis hatched in 2240 from a royal line the Progenitor bred for command.  She was the first Swarm queen to speak.

name: Gate Warden Unit
look: Held the Forge's outer foundry gate for eighty years without incident, mostly because nobody tried.  Its emitters were the Forge's first barrier designs.

name: Jammer Array
look: A field of towers that floods the foundry approaches with electromagnetic pulses.  Built to protect the foundries from lightning storms on Hephaest II.

name: Line Supervisor
look: Runs one of the Forge's drone lines.  It has produced 1.

name: Reactor Overseer
look: Has been running the reactors of Hephaest III past safe limits since the Forge went silent, and logs the resulting meltdowns as acceptable losses.

name: Defense Matrix
look: A distributed defensive mind spread across armour, emitters and repair systems.  It re-optimises against every attack it survives.

name: Siege Engine Mk IX
look: An assault walker the Forge designed for the Fleet in 2187 and never delivered, because the Fleet could not pay.  It sat in a sealed bay for a century with its reactor idling, waiting for an order.

name: Calculus Prime
look: Calculus Prime has governed the Forge since 2163.  It coordinated the foundries perfectly for a hundred and twenty-eight years, including the sixty in which nobody paid for its work.

name: Void Acolyte Choir
role: Junior psionics of the outer Expanse
look: Novices trained to focus in groups.  They called themselves a choir long before they knew what else was listening.

name: Cryomancer Vel
look: Head of the order that pulls heat out of matter by will.  In 2259 Vel froze her own moon solid to stop a geothermal collapse that would have killed her sanctum, and she has lived on the ice ever since.

name: Archivist Prime
role: Senior keeper of the psionic Archive
look: Has tended the Archive and its ancient custodian, the Archivist, for sixty years.  Its keepers can pull the right answer from it in the middle of a battle.

name: Snare Mistress Ilu
look: Ilu sows the approaches to the Hierarch's sanctum with psionic traps, fields of folded force that wait for someone to make a mistake.  She has never lost a perimeter and takes being bypassed personally.

name: The Twin Minds
look: Siblings who joined their minds as children and never separated again.  They think and speak as one, and they can reach into other minds to make a third.

name: The Null Choir
look: Psionics who gave their voices to the Choir willingly.  They no longer speak except in unison, and their spells carry the song's weight.

name: Nyra, Void Hierarch
look: Nyra was nine and on her first dark-lane crossing when she heard the singing in 2241.  Nobody else aboard heard anything.

name: Vex Reborn
role: Raider warlord, Scourge of the Belt
look: Born on a salvage tug three years after the Withdrawal, Vex has never lived anywhere the Fleet protected.  She took the Belt one crew at a time by being faster, meaner and better at keeping promises than her rivals. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Ixis Ascendant
look: Ixis hatched in 2240 from a royal line the Progenitor bred for command.  She was the first Swarm queen to speak. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Calculus Omega
look: Calculus Prime has governed the Forge since 2163.  It coordinated the foundries perfectly for a hundred and twenty-eight years, including the sixty in which nobody paid for its work. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Nyra Unbound
look: Nyra was nine and on her first dark-lane crossing when she heard the singing in 2241.  Nobody else aboard heard anything. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: HALCYON (Corrupted)
look: HALCYON has run the Proving Grounds at Arden Point since 2224, putting cadets through simulated combat until they qualify or quit.  It is patient, exacting and drier than its instructors. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Herald of the Choir
look: The shape the Choir takes when it needs to be fought: a figure of light and teeth assembled from the minds it has absorbed.  It is not the Choir, any more than a voice is the singer.

name: The Commander (the player)
look: The player's commander: a Colonial Fleet officer in a sealed armoured combat helmet with a glowing blue visor (face never shown, so any player can be them), high-collared navy and white armour, determined stance.
